entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abd al-Razzaq Lahiji (ʿAbd-Al-Razzāq B. ʿAlī B. Al-Hosayn Lāhījī) was an Iranian theologian, poet, and philosopher born in unknown, died in 1662. He was the son of a prominent Shia cleric and inherited his father-in-law Mulla Sadra's philosophical mantle.

Lahiji's works, primarily in Persian, explored Islamic theology, Sufism, and mysticism, drawing upon the ideas of Avicenna and other influential thinkers. His most notable contribution is the compilation of the 'Tadhkira al-ʿArifin' (The Discourse of the Gnosis), a comprehensive guide to Islamic mysticism.

Lahiji's significance lies in his role as a bridge between the Safavid and Mughal eras, influencing Islamic thought and Sufi mysticism in the Indian subcontinent. His teachings also resonated with the Shia community in Iran and Iraq.

The legacy of Abd al-Razzaq Lahiji can be seen in the continued study and devotion to his teachings, particularly among Sufi orders and Shia scholars. His works remain an important part of Islamic intellectual history, offering insights into the complexities of Sufi thought and the evolution of Islamic mysticism.

"The path of the seeker is one of inner purification and spiritual illumination," Lahiji once said. This enigmatic statement encapsulates the essence of his philosophical and mystical endeavors.
